apps.name: Ammy
apps.localizedDescription:
Ammy reads what you're playing in Apple Music — title, artist, album, cover art and the live playback position — and POSTs it as JSON to an HTTPS endpoint you choose. It keeps reporting while the screen is off and while other apps are in front: an update on every track change, and a heartbeat every 30 seconds.

BUILT TO PAIR WITH ISSUN, and not limited to it. Ammy has no opinion about what receives the data — anything that accepts an HTTPS POST works.

AMMY IS A SENDER, NOT A DESTINATION. On its own it does nothing: you need something running at the other end to point it at. Setup on the phone is an address and an optional key, and nothing else. Read the repo first.

Requires iOS 26 or later, and permission to read your media library.

versions.localizedDescription:
Make every app-affecting push a release, not just a tagged one

The manual "bump MARKETING_VERSION, git tag -a, push the tag" flow was
friction for its own sake once the actual goal became "get the latest
build onto my phone through SideStore" -- that only needs a push.

publish-source.yml now triggers on push to main (with build-ipa.yml's old
paths-ignore moved over, so a docs or relay-only commit still doesn't burn
a macOS build) instead of on a version tag, builds via workflow_call as
before, and creates a real GitHub Release with a synthesized tag
(v<marketing>-b<build>) rather than a human-authored one. The changelog is
read from the triggering commit's message instead of a tag annotation,
with git trailers filtered out since a subscriber reading What's New
doesn't need Co-Authored-By/Claude-Session lines.

build-ipa.yml drops its own push trigger -- publish-source.yml is now the
only thing that calls it, so a qualifying push builds once, not twice --
and always uploads the archived release artifact instead of only doing so
under github.ref_type == 'tag', which would otherwise silently break the
download step on every future run.

MARKETING_VERSION in project.yml is unchanged (still "1.0"); every build
from here just republishes under it, which build_source.py already
handles by replacing the previous entry for that version rather than
piling one up per build.
